title: Two Doors, Two Lies
summary: A known lie is a clue: flip it to find the truth.

steps.title: The puzzle
sentences: Two doors, one leads to treasure and one to a trap.
Door 1 has a sign: The treasure is behind this door. Door 2 has a sign: The treasure is behind door 1.
You are told both signs are lies. Which door has the treasure?
points: Two doors, one leads to treasure and one to a trap.

steps.title: How to think about it
sentences: If a sign is a lie, the opposite of what it says is true.
Take each sign and flip it.
points: If a sign is a lie, the opposite of what it says is true.

steps.title: The method: Flip the lies
sentences: Sign 1 lies, so the treasure is not behind door 1.
Sign 2 also lies, so the treasure is not behind door 1, which agrees.
With only two doors and none behind door 1, only door 2 is left.
points: Sign 1 lies, so the treasure is not behind door 1.

steps.title: The answer
sentences: Both flipped signs fit this answer.
Always check that your answer matches every clue.

quiz.q: A sign says: The treasure is behind this door, and it is a lie. The treasure is:
quiz.why: A lie means the opposite is true.
